body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-21 on the operator's own Kobo Clara BW (firmware 4.45.23792),
read-only copy of KoboReader.sqlite, mode=ro + PRAGMA query_only.

This is the #1657 fragment defect caught in the wild, on real user data, and it is
the concrete evidence that makes F-3e383a matter.

## The measurement

Applying #1657's own render predicate -- Nickel renders a Bookmark only when
Bookmark.ContentID exactly equals a content row with ContentType=9 -- to all 30
annotations on the device:

    Bookmark rows total              30   (17 highlight + 13 dogear)
    RENDERABLE (ContentType=9 match) 28
    NOT renderable                    2

The two that fail:

    The Able McLaughlins  dogear  created 2026-08-18T01:47:36
      ...!OEBPS!902696697345144105_59845-h-0.htm.xhtml#pgepubid00001
    The Age of Innocence  dogear  created 2026-08-18T01:51:09
      ...!OEBPS!7492349454248664808_541-h-0.htm.xhtml#pgepubid00008

Both carry a #fragment. A chapter identity with a fragment matches no ContentType=9
spine row, so Nickel cannot render the annotation anchored to it. That is exactly
the defect #1657 describes and #1773 fixes.

## Why this is F-3e383a's evidence, not a new bug

The forward fix has shipped. These two annotations are still broken because the
books were ALREADY DELIVERED to the device before it. F-3e383a is precisely the
finding that a KEPUB repair may never reach a device that already holds the book:
kepub_package_repair calls mark_book_modified(..., unsync=False), so
remove_synced_book -- the step whose own docstring describes it as what makes
every device re-pull -- never runs.

So the state on real hardware is: the defect is fixed for new deliveries, and two
of the operator's real annotations remain unrenderable on their device with no
mechanism to heal them. That is the gap F-3e383a names, now with a measured
consequence attached rather than a hypothetical one.

## Scope and honesty

- Both affected rows are DOGEARS, not highlights. All 17 highlights render.
  Impact is real but smaller than the raw 2/30 suggests -- a lost dogear is a lost
  place-marker, not lost user-authored text.
- I did NOT attempt a repair-and-redeliver to confirm the healing path, because
  that requires the armed F-3e383a experiment and a device sync, and a failed
  checkforchanges download makes Nickel replace the local annotation set with
  EMPTY. KoboReader.sqlite is read-only by standing rule, so a wipe would be
  unrecoverable. ASSUMED, not observed: that re-delivery would fix these two.
- Device-side capture kept out of the repo and deleted once it stops being evidence.

---
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-23 on the same device (read-only copy db-20260822-235633,
mode=ro + PRAGMA query_only). **The count is now 1, not 2.** The finding's own
predicate, re-run unchanged:

    Bookmark rows total              30   (17 highlight + 13 dogear)
    RENDERABLE (ContentType=9 match) 29
    NOT renderable                    1   <- was 2

The Age of Innocence dogear (BookmarkID 054fceb2-60a7-4658-bda4-25ace97e7688)
**lost its `#pgepubid00008` fragment on the device** and now matches a
ContentType=9 row exactly. Nothing was deleted: membership is identical across
snapshots (30 rows, same BookmarkIDs), and its StartContainerPath and
ChapterProgress are unchanged.

WHO DID IT -- narrowed, not closed:

* NOT a server push. The CWNG row for that annotation is untouched since
  2026-08-18 01:51:35 (`server_modified_at` unchanged, `content_revision` still
  1); every book on the deployed server is still `authority_status='unseeded'`
  and `config_kobo_two_way_annotation_sync = 0`. Containment held -- CWNG has
  never served an annotation GET for this book. [OBSERVED]
* The device row's `SyncTime` moved 2026-08-18T01:51:34Z -> 2026-08-21T04:56:35Z
  and its `DateCreated` moved 2026-08-18T01:51:09.113 -> 2026-08-18T01:51:35.410,
  i.e. it was rewritten locally, adopting a timestamp within ~300ms of CWNG's
  ingest time for the same annotation. [OBSERVED]
* The trigger is UNDETERMINED. [ASSUMED] It resembles the device-side ContentID
  rewrite in section 6 of KOBO-HIGHLIGHTS-STATE.md, but that case produced a bare
  `OEBPS/...` path and this produced a well-formed `<uuid>!OEBPS!...` identity, so
  it is not the same rewrite.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE COUNT: if a routine device-side mechanism strips
redundant fragments, the #1657 exposure is partly self-correcting and the tier-2
priority argument changes. Do not assume it either way. The closing experiment
uses a probe book, never the operator's real library: create a TOC-navigated
fragment-bearing dogear on a disposable synced book, snapshot, exercise the
candidate triggers one at a time, and re-snapshot after each.

The remaining non-renderable annotation is unchanged and still real:

    The Able McLaughlins  dogear  created 2026-08-18T01:47:36
      42258268-...!OEBPS!902696697345144105_59845-h-0.htm.xhtml#pgepubid00001
      ChapterProgress 0.5714  StartContainerPath OEBPS/...h-0.htm.xhtml#kobo.12.1

That book is already split into h-0..h-23, and `...h-0.htm.xhtml` does exist as a
ContentType=9 row, so the fragment alone is what breaks the match.

---
UPGRADED TO PHOTOGRAPHED HARDWARE EVIDENCE 2026-08-23, with a positive control
and complete page coverage. The earlier evidence was the render predicate
applied to the DB; this is the defect seen on the panel.

Method: opened `The Able McLaughlins` on the Clara BW, reached each position
only through the book's own Annotations panel (never by tapping a page corner,
which would have created a dogear), and measured ink coverage in the top-left
and top-right corner regions of each captured frame.

    frame                                    TL%    TR%   folded corner?
    CONTROL - fragment-free dogear, ch III   0.0   30.2   YES, drawn
    front-matter document page 1 of 4        0.0    0.0   no
    front-matter document page 2 of 4        0.0    0.0   no
    front-matter document page 3 of 4        0.0    0.0   no
    front-matter document page 4 of 4        0.0    0.0   no

The control matters: it is a dogear in the SAME book, on the SAME device, in the
SAME session, whose ContentID (`...h-3.htm.xhtml`) matches a ContentType=9 row
exactly. It draws. The fragment-bearing one does not, anywhere in its document.

This also closes the caveat in section 1(b) of KOBO-HIGHLIGHTS-STATE.md, which
correctly warned that an earlier negative may have been read off the wrong page.
Here the entire document is four pages and **all four were captured**, so there
is no page the marker could have been hiding on. The dogear's recorded
ChapterProgress of 0.5714 lands on page 3, which is likewise blank in both
corners.

USER-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR, also OBSERVED:

* The annotation IS listed in the Annotations panel, under the file-level
  heading `THE ABLE MCLAUGHLINS` rather than a chapter name -- consistent with
  section 4: without a resolvable fragment the device only knows which file the
  annotation is in.
* Tapping it in the panel moves to page 1 of 4 of that document, not to the
  recorded position.

So the harm is precise: the user can see that the bookmark exists and roughly
where, but the device cannot draw it and cannot return them to it.

DEVICE INTEGRITY: a snapshot taken immediately after this pass holds exactly 30
Bookmark rows (13 dogear, 17 highlight) with an unchanged BookmarkID set -- zero
added, zero removed. Nothing was written to the reader.
title: Two of the operator's real annotations are unrenderable on hardware: the #1657 fragment defect, measured in the wild
